A method to reconstruct voxel values on-the-fly from wavelet coefficients during rendering, avoiding pre-computation of the entire volume.

Given a wavelet coefficient with $k$ levels and a target voxel $(x_0, y_0, z_0)$, find the voxel (cube of size $1 \times 1 \times 1$) from the level $k$, $w_k$, whose reconstruction contains the target voxel.
Map indices $x_0, y_0, z_0$ to $x_k, y_k, z_k$ in $w_k$ by dividing $x_0, y_0, z_0$ by $2^k$.
Find the corresponding voxel in the other seven regions of the decomposed data (fHHH, fLLH, fHHL, fHLL, fLHH, fLHL, fLLH, fLLL).
Apply the inverse wavelet transformation to the above eight sub-cubes to reconstruct a new sub-cube with size doubled in each axis ($x_{k-1}, y_{k-1}, z_{k-1}$).
Repeat steps 2 and 3 until level 0 ($w_0$) is reached.
